history.alt_text: An industrial shipping crate and detached scanner module arranged on a concrete loading bay floor.
history.caption: The gap between physical goods receiving and digital order management accounts for a third of retail shrink.
history.title: Supply Chain Shrink Gap

style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render, asymmetric off-centre layout. An engineered modular shipping crate and a detached electronic receiving scanner module separated by a wide physical gap, resting on a weathered concrete floor in a warehouse loading bay. Matte muted polymer and brushed steel materials with moulding seams and deep contact shadows, slate grey and safety yellow palette. One directional key light raking across the parts throwing long cast shadows. Generous negative space, clear physical arrangement of recognizable engineered parts, no text, no embossed lettering, no bare geometry.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, words, logos, people, floating objects
rationale: Clay render perfectly abstracts the structural disconnect between physical receiving and digital systems. By constructing this as a physical assembly of a crate and disconnected ledger module in a loading bay, we visualize the systemic gap without relying on literal stock photography.
subject: an industrial shipping crate and detached scanner module on a loading bay floor
core_thesis: A third of retail loss occurs during supply chain receiving, yet software budgets fund order promises rather than verifying physical receipts.
core_conflict: Funding the promise of delivery vs securing the proof of physical receipt.
